stage_a.note: Tim maintains a bright, smiling expression and positive tone while revealing the product.
Tim speaks with clear excitement and energetic gestures when dismissing the old round keg.
Tim opens with a friendly, approachable greeting to the panel.

venture.description: A portable, square-shaped mini-keg system designed to fit efficiently in refrigerators and dispense draft beverages.
venture.note: The founder asks for $300,000 for 10% equity in the company.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tim presents SquareKeg, a portable mini-keg that fits in a fridge, and pours drinks for the panel.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond expresses amazement at the product demonstration.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Peter jokes that he likes Tim even without knowing him.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tim names the investors and identifies the specific drinks he has poured for each of them.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark suggests that the panel should do a toast with their drinks.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin agrees to the toast and the panel cheers.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tim asks Kevin what he thinks of his specific drink.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin accepts the drink, stating that it is really good.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin asks if the cartridge uses carbon dioxide gas.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tim clarifies that Kevin's drink is running on a new nitrogen product release.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond asks what the value is in putting mixed drinks into the keg.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tim explains the value for home use, allowing users to batch a gallon of cocktails for easy transport.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond acknowledges that the product allows anyone to serve themselves.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori points out that the current product does not accommodate wine.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin asks if it is possible to put wine in the keg.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tim confirms they have a wine product in development that will run on argon gas.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark asks Tim to explain how all the pieces of the keg fit together.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tim explains that the keg holds 128 ounces of beverage.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark notes that the capacity is almost equivalent to a twelve pack.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tim confirms that it holds just about a twelve pack.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tim continues explaining that users fill it, assemble the tap, and pressurize it with gas.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin asks if the drink stays good until it is completely finished.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tim confirms that the beverage remains good until finished.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin asks how to disassemble the keg to put in a different drink.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tim explains the threaded parts and the pressure release valve that must be turned before disassembly.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori jokingly asks Mark if he is sure he wants to try disassembling it.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark pulls the pressure release valve, causing a loud spray of gas.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tim jokes that he was trying to help Mark with the valve.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark laughs and remarks that he expected the gas to spray out.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin notes the high valuation and asks about their sales figures so far.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tim shares that they have sold over 4,000 units with lifetime sales over 1.4 million dollars.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin asks over what period of time those sales were achieved.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tim clarifies that the sales occurred over the course of a year.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark asks how much profit Tim has made from those sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tim admits a loss last year but projects profitability and strong net margins for the current year.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Peter asks for the retail price of the kegs.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tim states that the retail price is 259 dollars.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Peter asks how much it costs to manufacture the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tim explains the cost is 130 dollars and details their new manufacturing facility designed to lower costs.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Peter clarifies that he would buy this as a consumer for his home, not for a business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tim confirms that Peter's understanding is correct.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin asks if the product could potentially be used for a business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tim explains their direct-to-consumer focus but mentions the original vision was commercial before the pandemic shifted plans.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Peter asks Tim how he came up with the idea for the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tim shares his background as an idea guy and how he realized the inefficiencies of traditional round kegs.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond jokes about how often Tim wakes up early thinking of efficient ways to drink.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tim plays along with the joke, noting he was just lucky with the idea.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond decides to exit, stating he does not comprehend the value of the product despite it being cool.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin asks if he could put three bottles of wine in the keg with argon gas for two weeks.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tim confidently confirms that the scenario Kevin described is entirely possible.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin accepts the answer, calling it a cool idea.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori decides to exit, expressing interest in the future wine product but declining to invest now.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Peter decides to exit, stating he cannot see how he could help scale it into a great business.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark decides to exit, loving the product but feeling too clumsy with it to find a strategic fit.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin asks when the new wine product will be available.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tim answers that the wine product is coming in less than three months.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori jokingly asks why Tim did not share that timeline with her before she exited.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tim humorously admits that he simply failed to mention it.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin makes an offer of 300,000 dollars for 20 percent equity, intrigued by the wine application.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin negotiates his offer, explaining that Tim needs his help to blow the product up online.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tim counters Kevin's offer, asking if he would consider meeting in the middle at 15 percent equity.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin refuses the counter and maintains his offer of 20 percent, citing the work required.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tim accepts Kevin's standing offer.

decisions.note: Thinks the product is cool but does not comprehend the value of it.
Thinks it's cool but wants to wait until the wine product is figured out.
Cannot see how he could help scale it into a great business.
Loves the product and sees value but is clumsy with it and doesn't see a fit.
Intrigued by the wine application and wants to take a flyer on it.
Asks Kevin to meet him in the middle at 15% equity.
Refuses the counter, stating it's a simple product that will require work to blow up online.
